chunks: Drawing a charge pump circuit. The question: Draw a circuit for a charge pump.
The standard way to draw a charge pump is a voltage doubler with four switches. A flying capacitor sits in the middle, with two switches on each plate.
One pair of switches charges it from the input. The other pair stacks it on the input and connects it to the output. A capacitor and the load sit at the output.
Picture a ferry that shuttles between two docks. At the first dock it loads up from the supply.
At the second dock, it is lifted onto a platform at the supply level and unloads into the output tank.
The two docks are never used at the same moment, which matches how the two switch phases must never overlap.
The ferry analogy does not show the voltage stacking, which is the heart of the circuit.
The generic doubler. S1 and S2 are closed in 1 (charge), S3 and S4 in 2 (transfer). Top plate node is joined to both S1 and S4; bottom plate node to S2 and S3.
The I out source stands for the load.
Switches S1 to S4: four transistor switches that connect the flying capacitor's plates. Clock phases ( 1 , 2 ): the two alternating settings of the switches.
Non-overlapping: the two phases are never closed together, so the supply is never shorted. Top plate and bottom plate: the two sides of the flying capacitor.
Inverter: a variant that gives -V in at the output ("How a charge pump works").
Draw the input on the left, the flying capacitor in the middle, and the output capacitor and load on the right.
In phase one, close S1 (top plate to V in ) and S2 (bottom plate to ground), so the capacitor charges to V in .
In phase two, close S3 (bottom plate to V in ) and S4 (top plate to the output), so the output is 2 volts in . If S2 and S3 closed together, they would short the supply to ground.
That is the whole idea.
"Voltage doubler: flying capacitor in the middle. S1 connects its top plate to V in and S2 its bottom plate to ground in phase one, charging it to V in .
In phase two S3 connects the bottom plate to V in and S4 connects the top plate to the output, so the output is 2 volts in . Output capacitor and load to ground.
Non-overlapping clocks. The passive version uses two diodes and a clock-driven capacitor."
